title: Heartless hit-and-run suspect abandons own son in SoCal crash that killed two teens
text:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

Police are hunting a heartless hit-and-run suspect after he allegedly left his 11-year-old son in a burning wreck following a devastating SoCal crash that killed two teen girls.

A $1 million arrest warrant has been issued for Terry Lamar Easter, 50 — also known as “Capone” — for his involvement in the fatal car crash in Victorville on August 14.

Easter was allegedly driving one of two vehicles when they struck best friends Isabell DeLand, 16, and Maddalyn Dailey, 17, slicing the girls’ car in half while killing them instantly.

The suspect allegedly drove a Chevrolet Camaro while another driver who stayed at the scene drove a Dodge Charger.

Easter reportedly fled on foot and left his son in the passenger seat, whereas the other driver remained at the scene and was arrested on suspicion of vehicular manslaughter with gross negligence.

The accused hit-and-run driver is listed as being 5 feet 6 inches tall with black hair and hazel eyes according to an alert from the California Highway Patrol.

“Detectives believe Terry Easter to be armed and dangerous,” the warrant added.

An associate of Easter, Ryan Lewis, and his mother, Madge Wells, were also listed to as being wanted in connection to the fatal accident, but both have since been apprehended.

The teenage victims were best friends and were just a few houses away from their homes when the horrific crash occurred. They also attended the same high school.

“I heard the garage door close, and within a minute, I heard the impact and I automatically knew. It’s a death trap because there are no signals,” Dailey’s father told NBC4 as he recalled his daughter telling him she was dropping off DeLand.
